headline.calibration: Sealed exp_return is a 21-SESSION expectation of roughly +0.17% to +1.7%; pro-rata that is +0.008% to +0.08% per session. Realised single-session moves were 40x to 200x that magnitude in both directions. The books' EXPECTATIONS are not wrong in sign so much as they are not on the same SCALE as one day's noise -- a 21-day claim cannot be graded on a 1-day outcome, and the fact that our only forward evidence is 1-day outcomes is itself the finding.

3a_band_prior_v2_from_the_first_tracker_.question: If BAND_PRIOR v2 (EXP-RETURN-XS-1) had been live from the first tracker day instead of the 2026-09-02 seal, how would the admitted set have differed each day?
3a_band_prior_v2_from_the_first_tracker_.method: Replay of the BAND_PRIOR rules directly over each tracker day file. The tracker begins 2026-08-30 (NOT 2026-08-27 as the brief assumed) so the counterfactual can only run over 4 day-files / 2 tradable sessions. Clause inputs are re-derived from the day file (target_ratio = mean_target/close, rating = rec_counts weighted 5..1, drawdown = close/high_60d-1, catalyst = days_to_catalyst) and will not reproduce the seal exactly, which uses its own feature builder; treat the DELTA between v1 and v2 as the result, not the absolute counts.
findings: v1 (UPSIDE-BAND-DECON-1) had a priced opinion on 44 of 3,059 names (1.4%). v2 has one on ~2,836 (92.7%).
Names where the four clauses fire AND the prior is positive: 5 under v1, 55-58 under v2 -- an 11x wider opportunity set on every one of the four day-files.
Overnight turnover of the admitted set falls from 33.3% (v1, 08-31->09-01) to 8.5% (v2); 16.7% -> 13.1% on 09-01->09-02. v2 does what it was built to do: admission stops flipping overnight.
ZERO sign flips: v2 never reverses v1's opinion, it only extends it. The 3..5 band and the >=5 toxic band are identical in direction across versions.
FORWARD (n=2 sessions): v1 -0.93% then -3.79%; v2 +0.11% then -1.26%. v2 beat v1 on BOTH sessions, by +1.04pp and +2.53pp.
v2 restricted to median_dollar_volume >= $25m: +0.81% (hit 76%) then -1.77%. v1 has ZERO names above the $25m floor on either day -- v1's admitted set was structurally unbuyable at size.
COUNTER-EVIDENCE, stated plainly: RZLV sat in the 3..5 band under BOTH priors. Neither version of the band prior would have prevented the month's largest single loss.

findings: Prose beats numbers by +0.64 of terminal wealth; numbers_only is the only arm that loses money and the only one below the null.
But REAL prose beats FABRICATED prose by only +0.10, and ANONYMISING the true entities IMPROVED the result (1.756 vs 1.670). The gain is narrative STR/UCT/URE, not the events having happened.
Calibration is NEGATIVE in all four arms -- the model orders better than it prices.
It is a RIDGE at k=5 that collapses at k=10 (1.076, t 0.54).
The shuffled null is flagged informative in every arm, returning 1.423 for real against the arm's 1.670: most of real's wealth survives shuffling.

experiments.title: Decompose the stop
experiments.do: run move_decomposition.py AT THE STOP CHECK rather than overnight, and shadow-log two policies against every live position: (a) today's total-return stop, (b) a stop on the COMPANY COMPONENT only, market leg widened by the name's own beta. Shadow only -- (b) places nothing.
experiments.decision_rule: over 21 sessions, promote (b) only if it avoids more beta-driven exits than it misses company-driven ones AND terminal wealth is equal or better. Rank on TERMINAL WEALTH, not the mean.
experiments.guardrail: print the worst case before any promotion. Today each book is under 100% gross with a -13% to -18% worst case; a wider stop on uncapped gross is a bigger loss (paid for 2026-08-28).
experiments.why_it_matters: it separates a beta budget from a stock-selection loss, which is the entire difference between our two graded sessions
